newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan's CPC buys 30,000/T of naphtha at $200/tn.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's CPC buys 30,000/T of naphtha at $200/tn.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has bought through a tender 30,000 tonnes of heavy naphtha for October 21-31 delivery at around $200 per tonne, an official said on Tuesday.
The tender, which closed on Monday, sought fixed price offers on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Kaohsiung.
The official said CPC decided to buy the cargo of high naphthenic and aromatic (N+A) naphtha after saying earlier on Tuesday afternoon that it might cancel the tender.
"There is one reason why we are buying," he explained. "We have a requirement and prices are going up because of Iraq."
But he said the award price was "not so good" in comparison to previous awards.
CPC's last tender for naphtha was cancelled at the end of June due to lack of demand. The best offer for the August 11-31 delivery cargo was at $185.80 per tonne, c-and-f.
The official said CPC's next requirement will be for November delivery. --Singapore newsroom (+65-8703086)
